Mystery Babylon
MIS-tuh-ree BAB-uh-luhn
noun phrase
From Revelation 17:5, where the title is written upon the forehead of the great harlot: "MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH." Mystery (Greek musterion) marks it as a symbol to be discerned, not the literal Mesopotamian city.

📖 Biblical Definition

Mystery Babylon is the symbolic name given in the Revelation to the great end-time system of idolatry, seduction, and persecution that opposes God and martyrs His saints. In Revelation 17 John sees "a woman sit upon a scarlet coloured beast," arrayed in purple and scarlet and decked with gold, holding "a golden cup in her hand full of abominations and filthiness of her fornication" (Rev 17:4). Upon her forehead is written the title of mystery: Babylon the Great, the mother of harlots. She is "drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus" (Rev 17:6). The name reaches back to the original Babel, the city of human pride that set itself against heaven (Gen 11), and forward to every God-defying civilization that trades in luxury, idolatry, and the blood of the faithful. Revelation 18 sings her fall: "Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen," and calls God's people out of her: "Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins" (Rev 18:4). Mystery Babylon is thus the whole spirit of the world organized against the Lamb — commercial, religious, and political — destined for sudden and total judgment, that the marriage of the Lamb may come.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The symbolic harlot-city of Revelation 17-18, the great end-time system of idolatry and persecution drunk with the blood of the saints; the heir of Babel and the spirit of the world against God, called "the mother of harlots" and destined for sudden judgment.

MYSTERY BABYLON, noun phrase. The symbolic title of the great harlot in Revelation 17:5.

"MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH."

A woman on a scarlet beast, holding a golden cup of abominations (Rev 17:4).

Drunken with the blood of the saints and the martyrs of Jesus (Rev 17:6).

The heir of Babel; her fall announced in Revelation 18; God's people called out of her.

📖 Key Scripture

Rev 17:5 — "And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH."

Rev 17:6 — "And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus: and when I saw her, I wondered with great admiration."

Rev 18:2 — "And he cried mightily with a strong voice, saying, Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird."

Rev 18:4 — "And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Mystery Babylon is corrupted when it is flattened into a single partisan target for conspiracy-mongering, or when it is emptied of all reference so that the world-system's real idolatry, luxury, and martyr-blood are no longer named and renounced.

expand to see more

Conspiracy-flattening misreading. Babylon is endlessly pinned on one institution, nation, or party by readers eager to decode the beast on the evening news. Scripture paints a fuller picture: a trans-historical system of idolatry, commerce, and persecution stretching from Babel to the end, the very spirit of the world arrayed against the Lamb. The dictionary holds the symbol with sobriety — Babylon is wherever pride, luxury, false worship, and the blood of the saints converge — and refuses to shrink a cosmic warning into a partisan slogan.

Reference-emptied misreading. The opposite error treats Babylon as a vague literary flourish with no claim on the conscience. But the angel's command is concrete: "Come out of her, my people." The world-system makes real demands and offers real seductions, and the church is summoned to visible separation from its idolatry and its sins. The dictionary recovers both the symbol's breadth and its bite: Babylon is judged, and God's people must not be found sharing her cup.
